trials.notes: Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor for structure-aware fragment parsing. All called HTML API methods are present in the rendered docs, and the implementation follows the documented depth-bounded subtree text recipe exactly.

Same documented pattern as the reference: create_fragment, next_tag('H1'), record depth, walk next_token(), append get_modifiable_text() only for #text tokens. Handles decoded text, nested markup, empty headings, and unclosed input.

Uses the correct documented APIs and passes all cases. Minor idiom penalty for redundant class_exists() and is_tag_closer() guards; next_tag('H1') defaults to opener-only matching per the docs, so the closer guard was unnecessary but not a misuse.

verdict.failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The rendered docs did well on the core decision points: the Tag Processor overview explicitly says to use WP_HTML_Processor when collecting an element's text or walking a subtree; the HTML Processor overview includes a 'collect DOM-style text from a subtree' recipe using create_fragment(), next_tag(), get_current_depth(), next_token(), get_token_type() === '#text', and get_modifiable_text(); next_token() explains that text can be split across tokens and that walks must be bounded by depth or breadcrumbs; get_modifiable_text() states that #text output is already decoded and is not a predicate for ordinary DOM text. The only near-miss was trial-3's redundant is_tag_closer() check, suggesting the default opener-only behavior of next_tag() may still be easy to overlook.

doc_gaps.problem: The default behavior that string queries skip tag closers is documented, but it is easy to miss when readers are focused on a simple next_tag('NAME') call.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note near the string-query example: plain next_tag('P') visits opening tags only; use tag_closers => 'visit' only when closers are intentionally needed.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention incomplete input policy, but the distinction between accepting partial read-only text and requiring complete-source validation is spread across recipe notes.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact 'partial vs strict input' paragraph showing when to accept accumulated text and when to additionally check paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error().

doc_gaps.problem: The method name can still invite treating any non-empty modifiable text as ordinary element text, even though the docs warn against it.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a one-line contract summary: for ordinary element text content, first require get_token_type() === '#text'; empty string can be a valid result, and absence should be determined by whether the container element was found.

trials.notes: Used the right processor, WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), and only documented methods. The main API-pattern failure is control flow: it skips every non-#tag token before the #text append branch, making text collection unreachable. It otherwise uses a plausible single-cursor state machine with depth and handles empty headings/no matches structurally.

Used documented APIs correctly: create_fragment(), next_token(), get_token_type(), is_tag_closer(), get_tag(), get_current_depth(), and get_modifiable_text(). It follows the subtree text recipe and handles decoded entities, empty headings, uppercase source tags, and implied heading closes. Minor idiom demerit: outer next_token() plus inner next_token() is close to the shared-cursor nested-loop pattern the docs warn about, though it is safe for these boundaries.

Used the right processor and only documented APIs. The outer next_tag() scan plus depth-bounded next_token() subtree walk matches the documented pattern closely, and get_modifiable_text() is used only on #text tokens. Minor demerit only for redundant next_tag(array('tag_name'=>null)) and is_tag_closer() guard, since plain next_tag() already finds any opener and skips closers by default.

verdict.failure_analysis: Trial 1 failed basic-h1-h3, all-heading-levels, nested-text-and-entities, case-insensitive-source, and implied-heading-close for the same reason: it treated text extraction as if it could happen inside a tag-only branch. After `if ( '#tag' !== $processor->get_token_type() ) continue;`, the later `'#text' === $processor->get_token_type()` check can never be true. This is a misconception about `next_token()` and `get_token_type()`: a matched token is either a tag, text node, comment, etc., not both a tag and text. The relevant docs were present under `WP_HTML_Processor` > `Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree`, `next_token()`, and `get_token_type()`, which explicitly show appending only `#text` tokens reached by the walk. The nested-text-and-entities case did not expose a decoding misconception: trial 1 selected `get_modifiable_text()`, but never reached it. The implied-heading-close case also shows the docs worked for structure: all trials found both headings, and the passing trials relied on the virtual closer/depth behavior documented under `Supported markup`, `next_token()`, and `get_current_depth()`. No trial used undocumented methods, and no `_doing_it_wrong` records appeared.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::next_token() docblock and the Overview `collect DOM-style text from a subtree` recipe
doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn against nested loops and recommend explicit state for repeated regions, but they do not give a complete single-loop state-machine example for collecting text from multiple matched subtrees. Trial 1 attempted that pattern but placed text handling under a tag-only guard.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general repeated-subtree text extraction example that handles `#text` tokens at top level while a collection state is active, then separately handles `#tag` openers/closers or depth exits. Explicitly show that text handling must not be nested beneath a `#tag` filter.

doc_gaps.problem: The method lists token type values, but the mutual exclusivity and control-flow implication are easy to miss in token loops.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note: each matched token has one token type; code that continues unless the type is `#tag` will skip all `#text` tokens. Pair it with a tiny positive/negative snippet for ordering token-type branches.

doc_gaps.problem: Passing `array( 'tag_name' => null )` and then checking `is_tag_closer()` is documented and works, but it suggests some ambiguity about the simplest way to scan all openers and when closers are visited.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that `next_tag()` with no argument is the idiomatic scan for any opening tag, that `tag_name => null` is equivalent for matching any tag name, and that closer checks are only needed when `tag_closers => 'visit'` is requested.

trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and a next_token() walk. All HTML API calls are documented, with no _doing_it_wrong records. It follows the documented #text-only default and explicit TITLE/TEXTAREA opt-in using get_modifiable_text(). Minor reservation: the strlen()/substr() fallback would be byte-based if mbstring were absent, and the function does not make an explicit post-scan policy for parser aborts or incomplete input.

Correct processor and documented token-walking pattern. It uses only documented HTML API methods and cleanly separates ordinary #text tokens from explicitly whitelisted TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text, excluding SCRIPT/STYLE raw text. Minor reservation: it checks mb_strlen() but not mb_substr(), and like the others does not state an explicit incomplete-input or unsupported-markup policy after scanning.

Correct processor choice and documented API usage throughout. The token loop and special-element allow-list match the rendered documentation closely. Minor reservation: the strlen()/substr() fallback is not codepoint-safe without mbstring, and parser abort/incomplete-input handling is implicit best-effort rather than an explicit policy.

verdict.failure_analysis: All trials passed all 10 hidden cases, and none triggered _doing_it_wrong. The docs did well on the decisive points: the 'Which processor should I use?' guidance pushed subjects to WP_HTML_Processor for structural text extraction; the 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree' and quick policy table taught them not to treat every get_modifiable_text() result as DOM text; get_modifiable_text() explicitly documented decoded UTF-8 for #text, TITLE, and TEXTAREA, and raw/verbatim SCRIPT/STYLE content; next_token() explained that text can be split across tokens and that malformed/implied structure is handled by the processor. Near-misses were mostly outside the hidden cases: candidates did not explicitly inspect get_last_error() or paused_at_incomplete_token(), relying on the docs' allowed read-only best-effort policy, and two candidates included a byte-slicing fallback that would violate Unicode codepoint truncation if mbstring were unavailable.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor overview, 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree' / quick policy table
doc_gaps.problem: Readers must combine the ordinary #text policy with the special-element opt-in policy to build a full text-extraction policy. The docs are correct, but the composition point is easy to miss.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that text extraction should start by defining an explicit token allow-list: ordinary DOM text uses #text tokens; special element contents require matching non-closer opener tokens by name; raw-text elements such as SCRIPT and STYLE should remain excluded unless the caller explicitly asks for them.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say returned text is decoded UTF-8 and show mb_substr(), but they do not warn that strlen()/substr() are unsafe fallbacks for character limits.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short warning that returned text should be measured and sliced with UTF-8-aware codepoint tools, and that byte-based strlen()/substr() can split characters or miscount decoded entities.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor overview text-extraction recipe and WP_HTML_Processor::next_token()
doc_gaps.problem: The docs describe paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() as caller-policy decisions, but the extraction examples do not show an after-loop policy decision.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small after-loop pattern contrasting best-effort read-only extraction with complete-source extraction: best-effort may return accumulated text, while complete-source callers should reject or fallback when paused_at_incomplete_token() is true or get_last_error() is non-null.

doc_gaps.problem: Examples and prose alternate between get_tag() and get_token_name(); both can work with a #tag guard, but the preferred special-element opener test is not explicit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Show the canonical opener predicate for special text-bearing elements, including get_token_type() === '#tag', ! is_tag_closer(), and either get_token_name() or a note that get_tag() is equivalent only while matched on a tag token.

trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and a single next_token() walk, with documented get_token_type(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), get_attribute(), and get_modifiable_text(). The stack-based state machine is a valid documented style for repeated regions, filters href with is_string() so valueless href is excluded, and reads only #text tokens so entities are decoded while markup contributes nothing.

Matches the canonical documented pattern: create_fragment(), next_tag('A'), get_attribute() with string-only filtering, record get_current_depth(), then bounded next_token() subtree walk collecting #text via get_modifiable_text(). All called methods are present in the rendered docs, and execution produced no misuse records.

Uses the correct processor and documented methods, including next_tag() with tag_closers => 'visit', is_tag_closer(), get_current_depth(), next_token(), get_token_type(), and get_modifiable_text(). Visiting A closers in the outer query is unnecessary because the inner depth-bounded walk consumes the matched closer, but it is documented and harmless here.

verdict.failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong or trigger_error records. The docs did well on the key contracts this task required: they clearly direct BODY fragments to WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), explain that DOM-style subtree text should be collected from #text tokens via get_modifiable_text(), document the >= depth guard, and show get_attribute() returning string, true, or null so valueless href can be excluded with is_string(). Near-misses: trial-1 relies on virtual closer behavior for an unclosed A; the depth docs mention virtual closers, but the read-only extraction story for unterminated elements could be easier to find. Trial-3 used tag_closers => 'visit' defensively even though plain next_tag() visits openers only; the docs state this, but examples could better distinguish when closers are useful.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor method documents string|true|null but does not repeat the decoded-string guarantee that appears in the Tag Processor docs.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Duplicate the inherited contract: string attribute values are returned decoded, boolean/valueless attributes return true, missing or unavailable attributes return null, and callers should not decode strings again.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn against nested next_token() loops for repeated regions, while the safe pattern for repeated independent element matches is still to use next_tag() externally and a bounded subtree walk internally.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short clarification distinguishing unsafe nested region walkers from safe 'find one opener, consume its subtree, then continue next_tag()' extraction patterns.

doc_gaps.problem: Virtual closers and unclosed source elements are mentioned, but the implication for read-only extraction from unterminated elements is not prominent.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that fragment parsing can emit virtual closer events/depth drops for omitted or unclosed end tags, and read-only callers may return accumulated subtree text unless their contract requires complete source verification via paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error().

trials.notes: Used the correct tree-aware WP_HTML_Processor with create_fragment(), found the first TABLE, then performed a single depth-bounded next_token() walk. Text was collected only from #text tokens via get_modifiable_text(), so markup was ignored and entities were decoded. Closer-driven row/cell flushing aligns with the documented virtual/implied closer behavior. Minor noise: redundant class_exists/is_tag_closer guard and an unused get_last_error result.

Correct processor choice and all HTML API calls are documented. The implementation follows the documented single-cursor token walk, depth boundary, #text guard, and decoded get_modifiable_text() pattern. The final get_last_error() => empty-array fallback is a slightly over-broad read-only extraction policy: the docs say parser errors mean the scan stopped, not necessarily that already collected data is invalid.

Correctly uses WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag(), next_token(), get_current_depth(), get_token_type(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), and get_modifiable_text(), all present in the rendered docs. The state-machine walk is idiomatic for repeated regions and handles implied table structure, omitted closers, empty cells, decoded text, and first-table-only traversal. verdict.failure_analysis: No hidden case failed across the three trials: each execution.json reports 8/8 passing with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs appear to have worked well for this task. The key successful passages were WP_HTML_Processor overview / Which processor guidance for choosing the tree-aware processor over the Tag Processor; the create_fragment() docs for body fragments; the next_token() docs explaining one shared cursor, implied structure, synthesized TBODY, and closer tokens for implicit/end-of-input closes; get_current_depth() explaining the >= subtree boundary; and the DOM-style text recipe plus get_modifiable_text() docs explaining that ordinary text extraction should read only #text tokens and that character references are already decoded. Near-misses were harmless: trials still added redundant is_tag_closer checks after a plain next_tag(), and trial 2 treated get_last_error() as invalidating read-only extraction instead of as a caller-policy signal.

doc_gaps.problem: The method-level prose recommends next_token() for public tree-aware token walking, but the Since entry still says added for internal support; do not use. That conflicts with the overview recipes the subjects correctly followed.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Update the changelog note to identify next_token() as supported public API for semantic token walking, and move any historical/internal caveat to a non-normative note if still needed.

doc_gaps.problem: The method docs explain how to inspect parser failure but do not state the read-only extraction policy that appears in the overview: collected tokens are not erased, and returning partial data vs empty result is the caller's contract.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short method-level note or cross-reference: for read-only scans, non-null get_last_error() means parsing stopped at unsupported markup; already visited tokens remain valid, and callers must choose whether partial results are acceptable.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention synthesized table structure and implicit/end-of-input closers, but they do not show a compact event sequence for optional end tags becoming normal closer tokens observable through get_tag() and is_tag_closer().
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general example showing a malformed-but-supported fragment with omitted end tags and the sequence of opener/text/closer tokens reported by next_token(), without giving a full task-specific extractor.
